title: RBI Revives FCNR(B) Swap Window: Can It Attract NRI Inflows?
description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has reintroduced a special FCNR(B) swap window for banks to attract Non-Resident Indian (NRI) deposits. This mechanism allows .

faq.q: Who is eligible to open an FCNR(B) account?
faq.a: Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) and Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs) are eligible to open FCNR(B) accounts.

faq.q: What are the typical tenures for FCNR(B) deposits?
faq.a: FCNR(B) deposits typically have fixed tenures ranging from one year to five years.

faq.q: Is the interest earned on FCNR(B) deposits taxable in India?
faq.a: No, the interest earned on FCNR(B) deposits is exempt from income tax in India for NRIs. However, it may be taxable in your country of residence.

faq.q: How does the FCNR(B) swap window benefit NRIs?
faq.a: The swap window reduces the hedging cost for banks, allowing them to offer higher interest rates on FCNR(B) deposits, making them more attractive for NRIs.

faq.q: What currencies can FCNR(B) deposits be held in?
faq.a: FCNR(B) deposits can be held in major foreign currencies such as USD, GBP, EUR, JPY, and CAD.

faq.q: Can I withdraw my FCNR(B) deposit before maturity?
faq.a: Yes, premature withdrawals are generally allowed, but they may be subject to penalties as per the bank's terms and conditions.
